title and abstract.summary: The study measured the functional traits of plants and pollinators across 51 grasslands to explore the effects of honeybee abundance, temperature, plant functional diversity, and trait similarity between wild pollinators and the honeybee on the resource overlap between wild pollinators and the honeybee.

introduction.summary: The study discusses the functional traits of plants and pollinators, specifically mentioning the western honeybee, to help identify the likelihood, strength, and direction of interactions between managed and wild pollinators. This study investigated how the functional traits of plants and pollinators, along with the abundance of honeybees and temperature, affected the foraging behavior of wild pollinators. methods.summary: The study measured plant-pollinator interactions by calculating the CWM resource overlap between wild pollinators and the honeybee across different trait categories (e.g., body size) at various sampling sites.

results.summary: The study measured the interactions between 262 plant species and 325 pollinator species, detailing various measurements of plant and pollinator traits, such as proboscis length, body length, and flower corolla length, across 1497 unique plant-pollinator interactions. This study measured the resource overlap between wild pollinator communities and the honeybee (Apis) using various models incorporating different explanatory variables, including honeybee abundance, plant functional richness, and specific traits of pollinators like proboscis length and body size.
